translationRepairs: Prince Jianping of Yong'an, Jun, whose style name was Dingle, was the third son of Gao Huan.
Prince Jianping of Yong'an, Jun, whose style name was Dingyue, was the third son of Gao Huan.
字定樂 is the courtesy name; 定樂 is Dingyue, and “Dingle” is a false reading of 樂.
Prince Jianping of Yong'an, Jun, style name Dingle, was the third son of Shenwu.
Prince Jianping of Yong'an, Jun, style name Dingyue, was the third son of Shenwu.
The literal field likewise misreads 定樂 as Dingle; Dingyue restores the correct courtesy-name romanization.
Jun often rebuked those at the emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe his elder brothers' noses for them — on this account he came to be resented.
Jun often rebuked those at the emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe Second Elder Brother's nose for him — on this account he came to be resented.
二兄 is singular “Second Elder Brother,” and s0017’s tears anecdote concerns Wenxuan alone; plural “elder brothers” invents multiple patients.
Jun often rebuked those at the Emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe the elder brothers' noses for them — on this account he came to be resented.
Jun often rebuked those at the Emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe Second Elder Brother's nose for him — on this account he came to be resented.
Literal 二兄 is likewise one second elder brother, not plural elder brothers; the proposed singular restores the Chinese referent.

In the last years of Gao Yang's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "My two elder brothers were never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne their understanding has suddenly advanced.

In the last years of Gao Yang's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "Second Elder Brother was never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne his understanding has suddenly advanced.
二兄 with singular 不甚了了 / 識解頓進 / 登祚 names Wenxuan alone; “two elder brothers” and plural “their” are unsupported.

In the last years of Wenxuan's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "My two elder brothers were never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne their understanding has suddenly advanced.

In the last years of Wenxuan's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "Second Elder Brother was never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne his understanding has suddenly advanced.
The literal field repeats the plural mistranslation of singular 二兄; Second Elder Brother with singular “his” matches the Chinese.
He was caged in iron and shut in the underground dungeon with Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun.
He was caged in iron and shut in the underground dungeon with Jun, Prince of Yong'an.
與永安王浚 separates the title 永安王 from the personal name 浚, so “Yong'an Jun” is wrong; this unit has no 簡平, so the proposed “Prince Jianping” still invents the posthumous name.
He was placed in an iron cage and, together with Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun, was put in an underground dungeon.
He was placed in an iron cage and, together with Jun, Prince of Yong'an, was put in an underground dungeon.
The literal likewise must separate 永安王 from 浚 and must not insert 簡平, which is absent from this sentence.

When Prince Yanzong of Ande proclaimed himself at Jinyang, he had Liu Zi'ang draft a memorial to Jie: "The sovereign has fled, the ancestral temple hangs in the balance, the lords press us to act; we hold command only for the moment — in the end it must return to Your Highness."

When Prince Yanzong of Ande proclaimed himself at Jinyang, he had Liu Zi'ang draft a memorial to Jie: "The sovereign has fled, the ancestral temple hangs in the balance, the lords press us to act; we hold command only for the moment — in the end it must return to our uncle."
叔父 is paternal uncle; “Your Highness” drops the kinship term that the memorial explicitly uses.
Jie said, "I am a son of Gao Huan; of fifteen brothers I alone survive. To see the altars overturned and die today — I need feel no shame before our tombs."
Jie said, "I am a son of the Shenwu Emperor; of fifteen brothers I alone survive. To see the altars overturned and die today — I need feel no shame before our tombs."
In quoted speech Jie says 神武帝子; substituting the personal name Gao Huan changes what he uttered.
Asked why, Shi said, "A commoner without office needs no bow."
Asked why, Shi said, "A Han man without office needs no bow."
無官職漢 includes 漢; “commoner” omits that word, while “Han man” restores it.
Ning was the weakest of the princes. His consort Lady Wang, daughter of Wang Xia, Groom of the Crown Prince, had an affair with a household slave; Ning knew but could not stop her.
Ning was the weakest of the princes. His consort Lady Wang, daughter of Wang Qia, Groom of the Crown Prince, had an affair with a household slave; Ning knew but could not stop her.
王洽’s given name 洽 is Qia; Xia is the wrong reading.

He became chief minister of the Masters of Writing and junior tutor of the crown prince, then minister of works, grand commandant, grand marshal, governor of Si Province, grand tutor, Henan-route grand mobile headquarters, and recorder of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed duke of Wencheng, grand preceptor and grand preceptor of the realm — and again made governor of Ding Province.

He became chief minister of the Masters of Writing and junior tutor of the crown prince, then minister of works, grand commandant, grand marshal, governor of Si Province, grand tutor, Henan-route grand mobile headquarters, and recorder of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed duke of Wencheng, grand preceptor, and grand steward — and again made governor of Ding Province.
別封…太師、太宰 lists two offices: 太師 (Grand Preceptor) and 太宰 (Grand Steward); “grand preceptor of the realm” wrongly duplicates 太師.

He soon became Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and successively Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, Grand Marshal, Governor of Si Province, Grand Tutor, Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Henan Road, and Concurrent Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Wencheng Commandery, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Preceptor of the Realm — and again made Governor of Ding Province.

He soon became Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and successively Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, Grand Marshal, Governor of Si Province, Grand Tutor, Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Henan Road, and Concurrent Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Wencheng Commandery, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Steward — and again made Governor of Ding Province.
The literal likewise must render 太宰 as Grand Steward rather than a second Grand Preceptor.
